plan: In a second-price sealed-bid auction (Vickrey auction), bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of the number of competitors or their strategies. This is because you pay the second-highest bid, not your own bid, so bidding your true value maximizes expected profit - overbidding risks winning at a loss, and underbidding risks losing profitable opportunities. With my value at $10, I should bid exactly $10 to ensure optimal outcomes in this single-round auction.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy since you pay the second-highest bid, not your own bid. If I win, I pay the second-highest bid regardless of how high I bid above that. Bidding below my value risks losing profitable auctions; bidding above risks winning at a loss. With no prior history to suggest collusion or unusual behavior from Andy or Charles, the optimal strategy is to bid exactly my true value of $43.

In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy: you win whenever your value exceeds the second-highest bid (which is what you'd pay), and bidding higher risks paying more than the item is worth, while bidding lower risks losing profitable wins. With no prior history to suggest otherwise, and no incentive to deviate, I will bid exactly my value of $35 to maximize expected profit.
